findings.title: Unguarded access to first destinationCalendar crashes Google Meet fallback
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` whenever the event has no destination calendar (empty array or null, which is now a very common case — several call sites build `destinationCalendar: []`). The very next line dereferences it: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. For any booking whose location is Google Meet and whose organizer/event type has no destination calendar, this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the whole booking creation fails. Use optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: In `create()`, `referencesToCreate` now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously the non-calendar branch used `result.credentialId`, i.e. the video credential id returned by `createMeeting`. With this change every `_video` booking reference is persisted with `credentialId = null`. Cancellation code (`handleCancelBooking`: `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`) only deletes the meeting when that id is present, so video meetings will silently never be deleted on cancellation for all new bookings.

findings.title: updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId
findings.body: `updateLocation()` builds `referencesToCreate` from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but these results come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent()`, which never sets `externalId` or `credentialId` on its returned `EventResult` (only `createEvent` does). Both fields are therefore always `undefined`, whereas the previous code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` / `.credentialId`. The references written by `editLocation.handler.ts` will have no external calendar id or credential id, so subsequent updates/deletes of that booking will target the credential-less legacy path / the "primary" calendar instead of the real destination calendar.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents can call updateEvent with an undefined credential
findings.body: Inside the new per-reference loop, when `reference.credentialId` is set but neither `this.calendarCredentials` nor the DB lookup yields a usable credential (e.g. credential deleted, or `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` missing), `credential` stays `undefined` and `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)` is still pushed. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` dereferences `credential.appName`/`credential.type` when building its result, throwing a TypeError. Because `return Promise.all(result)` is not awaited inside the `try`, that rejection escapes the surrounding try/catch and surfaces as an unhandled rejection rather than the intended degraded result. Skip the reference when no credential could be resolved.

findings.title: Error diagnostics removed from updateAllCalendarEvents catch block
findings.body: The catch block still computes the detailed `message` string but the `console.error(message)` call was deleted, so `message` is now dead code and calendar update failures are swallowed completely with no log output. Debugging multi-host calendar failures (the exact scenario this PR targets) becomes impossible; keep a log statement.

findings.title: updateEvent destination-calendar fallback can never match
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === undefined/""` and always returns `undefined`. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Result: for bookings whose reference has no `externalCalendarId` (legacy bookings, and references created by `updateLocation`, see above), `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, so the Google request is malformed and the update fails instead of hitting the host's destination calendar. Should fall back to the first destination calendar's `externalId`.

findings.title: deleteEvent destination-calendar fallback can never match
findings.body: Same inverted predicate as in `updateEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always resolves to `undefined` and `calendarId` degrades to `"primary"`. Events that live in a non-primary destination calendar and whose booking reference lacks `externalCalendarId` will no longer be deleted (Google returns 404, which the handler swallows), leaving orphaned calendar entries.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined` (when no destination calendar matches `credentialId`); the insert call guards this with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` that writes the Meet link into the description does not. When `selectedCalendar` is undefined the patch request is malformed and the event description will be missing the hangout link. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value for the patch.

findings.title: createEvent now ignores destination calendars that have no credentialId
findings.body: The target calendar is resolved exclusively via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable and is null for rows created before credential linking, so for those users the event is now written to `"primary"` instead of their configured destination calendar — a behaviour regression from the previous `destinationCalendar.externalId` lookup. Worse, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` still records `externalId: destination.externalId` in the booking reference for the credential-ful branch, so the stored reference can disagree with the calendar actually used, breaking later update/delete.

findings.title: Organization slug condition inverted (unrelated change)
findings.body: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting the condition. With team billing enabled the org now gets both a real `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` (the requestedSlug flow exists precisely because the slug must not be claimed until payment), and with billing disabled (self-hosted default) the organization is created with no slug at all, so org subdomain resolution breaks. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and should be reverted.

findings.title: Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when there is no primary destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and the collective handling is `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With optional chaining on `null`, the push is a no-op, so for a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but other hosts do, none of the host calendars are used — exactly the multi-host case this PR is meant to fix. Initialise the field to an array (or assign the collected list) instead of relying on `?.push`.

findings.title: Invalid dynamicUserList surfaces as a 500 instead of 400
findings.body: `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is thrown inside the new `try` in `loadUsers`, but the catch only maps `HttpError` and Prisma errors to a 400; everything else becomes `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. A malformed client request (empty dynamic user list) is therefore reported as a server error and the actual reason is lost. Throw an `HttpError` with status 400 directly.

findings.title: organization relation removed from the dynamic-booking user select
findings.body: In the `!eventTypeId` (dynamic group booking) branch of `loadUsers`, the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` sub-select was dropped. Any downstream consumer of `user.organization` for dynamic bookings (e.g. building org-scoped booker URLs) will now see `undefined`, and the two branches of `loadUsers` return structurally different user shapes, which weakens the inferred type the comment claims to rely on. Re-add the select unless you have verified no consumer reads it.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation now issues duplicated delete calls per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring branch (iterate all of the user's calendar credentials × all `updatedBookings`' first calendar reference) was moved inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references on a booking the whole credential×booking deletion matrix is executed N times, sending the same `deleteEvent` request repeatedly to each provider (and pushing N× duplicate promises into `apiDeletes`). For multi-host collective recurring events this multiplies external API calls and the risk of rate limiting. Hoist the recurring handling out of the per-reference loop.

findings.title: Credential-less destinations create events in every credential of that integration
findings.body: For each destination without a `credentialId`, the code creates an event in every calendar credential of the matching integration type (`this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)`). Now that `destinationCalendar` is an array and is populated with each collective host's calendar, two hosts with credential-less Google destination calendars cause 2 × (number of google credentials) event creations, i.e. duplicate calendar entries for the same booking. Additionally the resulting `EventResult`s carry no `externalId`, so the persisted booking references lose the external calendar id. De-duplicate destinations and pass the destination's `externalId` through.

findings.title: No tests for the array-based destinationCalendar behaviour
findings.body: This PR changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array across ~20 files and adds new branching in `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` (per-destination credential resolution, DB credential fallback, collective host aggregation), yet no unit/integration tests were added and the only test touched is an e2e expectation value. Given the number of null/empty-array edge cases introduced (see the Google Meet crash and the dropped collective calendars), at least tests covering: empty destinationCalendar, destination without credentialId, and a collective event with two hosts, are needed before merge.
